summary: Cambodia's eVisa portal issues the tourist visa online for 30 USD and a one-month stay; the UK, Canadian and Australian governments say their citizens can also get one on arrival. ASEAN citizens enter visa-free. All travellers can submit the free Cambodia e-Arrival card within 7 days before arrival; Cambodia's eVisa portal says all travellers are required to fill it in, even visa holders.

declarations.name: Cambodia e-Arrival Card (CeA)
declarations.text: Cambodia's e-Arrival card combines the immigration, customs and health declarations in one online form (web or Cambodia e-Arrival app). The portal says all travellers can submit it within 7 days before their arrival and that submission is free; it lists Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville international airports. Cambodia's eVisa portal says all travellers are required to fill in the e-Arrival even if they have been granted a visa, and Canada's travel advice says the forms must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

currencyLimits.text: Cambodia's Law on Foreign Exchange requires a traveller bringing in or taking out means of payment of USD 10,000 or more in foreign currency, or the equivalent in riel, to declare them to customs at the border.

source.name: National Bank of Cambodia — Law on Foreign Exchange (22 August 1997), English text

notes: Canada's travel advice says the Cambodia e-Arrival forms cover immigration, customs and health, and must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

The customs step of Cambodia's e-Arrival form lists the personal duty-free allowances as 2 litres of alcohol, 200 cigarettes, 50 cigars, 250 sticks of tobacco and 35 ml of perfume, and says passengers under 18 get the perfume allowance only. It also asks whether you carry foreign currency or monetary instruments worth over USD 10,000, and warns that carrying illicit drugs can bring life imprisonment.

safety.text: The UK advises against all but essential travel within 20 km of the land border with Thailand, where landmines and unexploded ordnance also remain; Canada and Australia advise against all travel within 50 km of it, and the land crossings with Thailand are closed. Australia advises a high degree of caution in the rest of the country. The UK warns that most thefts are bag snatchings, often by thieves on motorbikes, and that organized crime groups run job scams advertising easy, well-paid work. Mined areas are often unmarked: the UK says not to stray off main routes in rural areas.

tips.text: The official eVisa site, run by Cambodia's foreign ministry, is evisa.gov.kh.
Bring US dollar notes in good condition: Canada's travel advice says only newer, undamaged notes are accepted, and Australia's Smartraveller says sellers may refuse dirty, torn or high-value notes.

The Cambodia e-Arrival card is free and is submitted within 7 days before arrival, at arrival.gov.kh or in the official Cambodia e-Arrival app. Cambodia's eVisa portal says all travellers are required to fill it in, even visa holders.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Cambodia?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states the rule for US passport holders, so this page shows none. Cambodia's eVisa portal issues the tourist visa (Visa T) online for USD 30, for a one-month stay; its tourist-visa page lists ASEAN nationalities under 'Visa Exemption' and does not mention the United States. Canada's travel advice says a visa may be extended only once.

faq.question: Is the Cambodia eVisa better than the visa on arrival?
faq.answer: The eVisa costs 30 USD; no official source we could read states the visa-on-arrival fee. Canada's travel advice says tourist and business visas allow 30 days, that the visa on arrival is issued at international airports and major land border crossings, that no photo is needed and that the fee can be paid by card, though cash may be needed if electronic systems are down; the UK Foreign Office says that if you do not get an e-visa you can get a visa on arrival at airports or land border crossings, and that you need to provide a photo and pay in US dollars. The eVisa is accepted only at the Techo (Phnom Penh), Siem Reap Angkor and Sihanoukville airports and the Bavet and Tropaeng Kreal land crossings — Cham Yeam and Poipet on the Thai border are temporarily closed to eVisa entry — so check your entry point first.

faq.question: What is the Cambodia e-Arrival card?
faq.answer: The Cambodia e-Arrival (CeA) is a free online form combining immigration, customs and health declarations, submitted within 7 days before arrival at arrival.gov.kh or via the Cambodia e-Arrival app. The portal says all travellers can submit it, and Cambodia's eVisa portal says all travellers are required to fill it in even if they have been granted a visa; Canada's travel advice says it must be completed within 7 days of your scheduled arrival.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Cambodia?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says you can extend a tourist visa while in Cambodia. Canada's travel advice says visas must be renewed for stays over 30 days and may be extended only once. No official source we could read states the length of an extension of an extension.

faq.question: Which nationalities enter Cambodia visa-free?
faq.answer: Cambodia's list of visa exemptions, published by its embassy in London, gives ordinary passport holders of ASEAN countries visa-free entry: 30 days for Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Laos, Singapore and the Philippines, 14 days for Thailand, Myanmar and Brunei. Maldivian (30 days) and Seychellois (15 days) ordinary passports are also exempt.
